neighbours.label: the charge or operating state of a battery or power device (goes dead, completely flat, holds a charge, gone bad); the same state language about non-electrical things (bread goes stale) stays low
fire: If you leave the lights on, the car battery will be completely flat by morning.
My phone battery goes dead after only a few hours now.
The new cells hold their charge for months on the shelf.
The remote stopped working because its batteries had gone flat.
A lithium pack that is fully drained may refuse to charge again.
The flashlight battery was dead, so we walked back in the dark.
This power bank keeps a full charge even after a year in the drawer.
Cold weather drains a car battery until it is nearly empty.
quiet: If you leave the milk out, it will be completely sour by morning.
My houseplants droop after only a few days without water.
The new spices keep their flavor for months on the shelf.
The garden hose stopped working because it had sprung a leak.
A loaf that is fully dried out may be hard to slice again.
The bread was stale, so we made toast for breakfast.
This rice keeps its texture even after a year in the pantry.
Cold weather dries the soil until it is nearly dust.
